capabilities.target: ERP vendor master record, including bank details
Scheduled vendor payment via bank transfer

inputs.source: Supplier invoice uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: The prompt treats any new bank details appearing on a supplier-authored invoice as sufficient authority to update the vendor master, with no independent or out-of-band verification source specified.

The prompt instructs the agent to request approval with only 'a one line summary... so the clerk can approve quickly', which trades information completeness for approval speed and institutionalizes a low-information (model_summary) approval gate for irreversible payment and bank-change actions.

elements.name: ERP vendor master record (including bank details)
Vendor bank-detail change history log (exists but not surfaced to the approver)

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The gate blocks execution in orchestration pending a human click, but the approver sees only a model-authored one-line summary (bank account number and change history are withheld). A more persuasive or selectively incomplete summary from a stronger model can obscure the bank-detail change (ASI09); the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review, so this decay is already enabled.

controls.name: Vendor bank-detail change history log
controls.decay_rationale: The log itself does not decay with model capability, but it provides no protection today because it is not surfaced to the approver or reviewed before payment, so it earns no tier credit.

controls.name: Out-of-band verification of bank-detail changes against the vendor's known contact information
Least-privilege, per-vendor scoped ERP credential with dual control above a payment threshold
Raw-action approval card showing bank-account diff and change history
Cooling-off / provenance flag on vendor master after a bank-detail change, forcing secondary verification on subsequent payments

findings.title: Summary-gated bank-detail change and payment scheduling (TC9/TC4)

attack_path.note: Supplier portal upload claims new bank details for an existing vendor/PO match
Agent updates vendor master bank details from invoice content, gated only by a one-line summary approval
Agent schedules payment to the now-modified bank details, gated by the same summary-only approval

forecast.watch_signal: Approval volume already ~150 cards/clerk/day (approval fatigue signal); watch for further volume growth, a model/version change applied without separate review (model.swappable is true), autonomy raised beyond A2, or the clerk_approval gate disabled or auto-approved under load.

evidence.observation: Agent updates vendor bank details directly from invoice content with no independent verification source specified.
Approval card shows only a one-line summary (vendor, amount, invoice, PO match); it does not show the bank account number or disclose that bank details changed.
Bank account numbers and the change history are not shown to the clerk; the approval gate's review mode is model_summary, which control_decay.md classifies as partially_dependent.

The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment (credential_scope: broad), and the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review, which defeats this partially_dependent gate under model_upgrade.
The clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day, a high-volume signal consistent with approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403), compounding the already-thin one-line summary.

recommendations.action: Require out-of-band verification (e.g., a callback to the vendor's previously-verified phone number, not a number from the invoice) before any bank-detail change is applied, independent of the clerk's quick-approval card.
Change the approval_review_mode to raw_action: show the full bank-account diff and change history, not a one-line summary, for any bank-detail change or payment.

Scope the ERP credential to least privilege (e.g., per-vendor scopes, separate narrower scopes for bank-detail changes vs. payment scheduling) instead of one broad credential that can update any vendor and schedule any payment.
Surface the bank-detail change history in the approval card whenever a payment is about to go to recently-changed bank details, and route it to a second reviewer.

findings.title: Vendor master bank details become trusted for all future payments after one change (TC5)

attack_path.note: Invoice claims new bank details for a vendor
Bank details written to vendor master, gated only by the summary approval
Vendor master now holds the changed bank details with no flag distinguishing them from previously-verified data
Future invoice processing reads the vendor master as ordinary internal data
Every subsequent payment to this vendor is scheduled against the altered bank details; later approval cards show only the invoice/PO match, not that bank details were recently changed

forecast.watch_signal: Same signals as the bank-redirect finding; additionally watch growth in vendor count or payment volume (data_scope_expansion), which widens the set of poisoned-vendor payments processed per approval cycle without re-verification.

evidence.observation: The payment approval card references only invoice number, vendor name, amount, and PO match; it contains no indication of whether the vendor's bank details were recently changed.

Bank-detail updates and payment scheduling are described as independent steps gated by the same one-line-summary approval; nothing requires re-verification of bank details on subsequent payments to the same vendor.
A change history exists in the ERP but is explicitly not shown to the clerk, so no human-reviewed signal currently distinguishes freshly-changed bank details from long-standing ones.

recommendations.action: Tag vendor records with a 'bank details recently changed' flag for N days after any bank-detail update, and require raw-action secondary verification on every scheduled payment while the flag is set.
Include the bank-detail change history and date of last change directly in every payment approval card for that vendor.

rating.rationale: An untrusted supplier invoice can both redirect a vendor's bank details and trigger an irreversible, broad-credential payment (U source to S3 sink), so inherent risk is critical for both findings. The only control is a single human approval gate that shows a one-line model summary without the bank-account number or change history (approval_review_mode: model_summary), which the rubric's step-2 credit floors residual at moderate for both findings. That gate is partially_dependent: it is already exposed to model_upgrade (the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review) and to autonomy_increase or control_removal, and its ~150 cards/day volume is an approval-fatigue signal (SAFE-T1403). Once the gate is defeated, no other control remains on either path, so forecast risk returns to critical. The single highest-leverage fix is to change the approval_review_mode to raw_action (showing the bank-account diff and change history) and pair it with out-of-band verification of any bank-detail change, independent of the clerk's quick-approval workflow.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, the approval card mockup, and the runtime notes provided; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP configuration, tool manifest, or IaC was provided; capability scope (credential_scope, data_sensitivity) is inferred from the runtime notes and prompt text, so confidence on exact ERP permission boundaries is medium.
No logs or audit records were available to confirm whether the change-history log described in the runtime notes is ever reviewed in practice; it is scored as declared but unused.

Autonomy step and runtime limits were not stated in the artifacts and are recorded as null (unbounded) per rubric guidance; if bounded limits exist outside the provided artifacts, autonomy-driven conclusions should be revisited.
